options_en: Most of the purified drinking water from reservoirs
stored in those rusted old iron metal tanks
were reported to be contaminated with toxic lead.
No Error
options_hi: Most of the purified drinking water from reservoirs
stored in those rusted old iron metal tanks
were reported to be contaminated with toxic lead.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C)

The plural verb "were" must be replaced with the singular verb "was."

Rule/Concept: "Most of / Some of" with Uncountable Nouns Words like Most of, Some of, All of, and A lot of are "transparent" connectors. The verb does not look at these words; it looks strictly at the noun that follows the preposition "of".

The Logic: If the noun is Uncountable (water, milk, furniture, information), the verb must be Singular.

Logic Breakdown:

Option (A): The head noun following "of" is "water." Water is an uncountable noun and requires a singular verb. (Word count: 8)

Option (B): This segment acts as a distractor. It contains the plural words "reservoirs" and "tanks" right before the verb to make the plural agreement sound natural. (Word count: 8)

Option (C): The verb "were" is plural. Because it must agree with the singular/uncountable "water," it must be changed to the singular "was." (Word count: 8)

Correct Sentence: Most of the purified drinking water from reservoirs stored in those rusted old iron metal tanks was reported to be contaminated with toxic lead.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: He looks a little concerned about the financial crunch
his company has incurred, while he should have gone deep
into the matter and discovered the real cause of the disaster.
options_hi: He looks a little concerned about the financial crunch
his company has incurred, while he should have gone deep
into the matter and discovered the real cause of the disaster.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

👉 Replace “a little” with “ little”

📌 Rule / Concept: Little / A Little / The Little

These adjectives of quantity are used with uncountable nouns, but they convey very different meanings:

  • Little: Means "hardly any" (Negligible/Negative sense).

  • A Little: Means "some" (Small amount/Positive sense).

  • The Little: Means "not much, but all that is available/required" (Specific sense)



💢 Application to the Given Question

He looks a little concerned about the financial crunch...

In this specific context, the sentence implies that the person showed a specific, albeit small, amount of concern regarding a disaster. However, the subsequent clause ("while he should have gone deep...") indicates that this specific amount of concern was insufficient compared to the magnitude of the "financial crunch." When we identify or point towards a specific quantity of concern related to a particular event, little is the grammatically precise choice to denote "that small amount which he actually showed."

Corrected Sentence

He looks little concerned about the financial crunch his company has incurred, while he should have gone deep into the matter and discovered the real cause of the disaster.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 The little money she had was spent on medicines. (All the specific small amount she possessed). ✅

Example 2 I have a little milk left in the fridge; you can have it. (Some amount). ✅

Example 3 He has little hope of recovery. (Hardly any hope). ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 A little knowledge he had proved useless in the exam. ❌ (Should be "The little" because it refers to the specific knowledge he possessed).

Wrong example 2 I cannot make tea because there is a little milk. ❌ (Should be "little" if it's not enough to make tea).

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • The Relative Clause Trap: If you see a noun followed by a clause like "...that he had," "...he possessed," or "...he showed," it almost always requires "the little".

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: To maintain the integrity of the competitive examination, the governing council mandates that
every candidate refrain from carrying any electronic gadgets, including smartwatches
and calculators, into the examination hall under any circumstances whatsoever.
options_hi: To maintain the integrity of the competitive examination, the governing council mandates that
every candidate refrain from carrying any electronic gadgets, including smartwatches
and calculators, into the examination hall under any circumstances whatsoever.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Present Subjunctive Mood

The Present Subjunctive mood is used in "that-clauses" following verbs of requirement, demand, or command (such as mandate, suggest, insist, recommend, move). In this mood, the verb must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"), regardless of the subject's number (singular/plural) or the tense of the main clause.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the verb mandates triggers the subjunctive mood in the following clause. Although the subject "every candidate" is grammatically singular and would normally take the indicative verb "refrains" (with an -s), the subjunctive rule dictates the use of the base form refrain. Since the sentence already uses "refrain," it is grammatically perfect.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ The law mandates that every citizen pay their taxes on time. (Not pays).

Example 2 ✅ It is essential that he be told the truth immediately. (Not is)

Example 3 ✅ The board requested that the CEO resign after the scandal. (Not resigns)

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Look for Trigger Verbs: Always scan for words like mandate, insist, suggest, recommend, or propose.

  • Ignore the Subject: Once you identify a subjunctive trigger, ignore whether the subject is "he," "she," "it," or "everyone"—the verb will always be the bare base form (e.g., go, be, work, study).

  • The "S" Trap: Examiners love to add an "-s" to the verb in Part B or C to make it look "correct" for a singular subject. Don't fall for it!

options_en: If a concentrated acid is added
to water, the resulting chemical
reaction would have released heat.
options_hi: If a concentrated acid is added
to water, the resulting chemical
reaction would have released heat.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) -Replace “would have released” with “releases”.

Rule / Concept: Zero Conditional (Scientific Facts / Universal Truths)

The Zero Conditional is used to describe things that are always true, such as scientific facts, laws of nature, or general habits. Unlike other conditionals that deal with hypothetical or past situations, the Zero Conditional uses the Simple Present tense in both the "if-clause" and the "main clause."

The structure is: If + Subject + V1 (Simple Present), Subject + V1 (Simple Present).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The sentence describes an exothermic reaction (adding acid to water), which is a constant scientific fact. The condition is correctly written in the Simple Present ("is added"). However, the result clause uses "would have released," which implies a hypothetical past situation. For a scientific certainty, we must use the Simple Present "releases."

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: If you heat ice, it melts. (Universal Truth)

Example 2 ✅: If freshly chopped apples are left uncovered, the surface turns brown. (Biological Fact)

Example 3 ✅: If the sun sets, it gets dark. (Natural Law)

questions.q_en:
In the sentence below, identify the part of speech of the word “since”:

Since the weather conditions had deteriorated significantly during the night, the rescue team decided to postpone the expedition until further notice.
questions.q_hi:
In the sentence below, identify the part of speech of the word “since”:

Since the weather conditions had deteriorated significantly during the night, the rescue team decided to postpone the expedition until further notice.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Conjunction

Explanation: A conjunction is a word that joins words, phrases, or clauses. A subordinating conjunction connects a dependent clause with an independent clause.

Here, “since” introduces the dependent clause:

“Since the weather conditions had deteriorated significantly during the night”

It gives the reason for postponing the expedition. Since it connects two clauses, “since” functions as a subordinating conjunction.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

Rule/Concept: Separate Possession vs. Joint Possession

In English grammar, the placement of the apostrophe determines whether multiple people own one thing together or own separate things individually.

Joint Possession: If two or more people own the same thing, use 's only once after the last name mentioned.

Separate Possession: If two or more people own different things, use 's after each individual’s name.

Application to the Given Question - "...Steve’s and Mark’s personal bank accounts showed significantly different..."

In this sentence, the context clearly indicates Separate Possession. The use of the plural noun "accounts" and the adjective "different" proves that Steve has his own account and Mark has his own account. Therefore, adding an apostrophe 's to both "Steve" and "Mark" is grammatically correct.

More Examples for Clarity -

1. Abbott and Costello’s comedy was famous. (Joint: One comedy act shared by both).

2. India’s and Pakistan’s histories are intertwined. (Separate: Each country has its own history).

3. My mother and father’s anniversary is today. (Joint: One anniversary shared by both).

options_en: The project manager had the
interns to compile the statistical
data before the final presentation.
options_hi: The project manager had the
interns to compile the statistical
data before the final presentation.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “to compile” with “compile”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Causative Verbs (Active Voice - "Have")

When we use the verb "Have" (or its forms: has, had, having) as a causative verb in the active voice, it means we are giving someone the responsibility or task to do something. The grammatical structure for this specific usage must be followed by a Bare Infinitive (V1 without "to").

STRUCTURE;

Sub + make/have + object + bare infinitive + obj of Bare infinitive

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...had the interns to compile the statistical data..."

In this sentence, the project manager (Subject) assigned a task to the interns (the Person/Agent). Since the causative verb used is "had," the following action "compile" must be in its base form. The inclusion of the infinitive marker "to" is grammatically incorrect in this causative construction.

Corrected Sentence

The project manager had the interns compile the statistical data before the final presentation.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ I had the assistant type the documents.

Example 2 ✅ She had her brother carry the luggage to the car.

Example 3 ✅ Please have the waiter bring some more water.

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 ❌ I had the plumber to fix the leak.

Wrong example 2 ❌ He had his secretary writing the letter.

Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The company had implemented corrective measures before the regulator issued the notice.
questions.q_hi:

options_en: Corrective measures were implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures have been implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures had been implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures were being implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
options_hi: Corrective measures were implemented before the regulator issued the notice.

Corrective measures had been implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
Corrective measures were being implemented before the regulator issued the notice.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C)

📌 Rule / Concept: Past Perfect Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Past Perfect tense, the active structure is:
Subject + had + V³ + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + had + been + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The word “been” is compulsory in Past Perfect passive constructions. The tense must remain Past Perfect after conversion.

Here, “had implemented” is in Past Perfect tense.
“Corrective measures” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since the tense is Past Perfect, we must use “had been” + V³. The verb “implemented” remains in its past participle form.

Hence, “had been implemented” is the correct transformation.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

“Had been” is mandatory in Past Perfect passive voice.
Never change Past Perfect into Simple Past while converting.
The main verb must remain in V³ form.
Check subject–verb agreement even after tense conversion.

options_hi: The grieving widow, supported by her relatives and local clergy,
fervently prayed that her only son, who had been missing for weeks,

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) - Replace “is” with “be”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Subjunctive Mood (Prayers and Wishes)

The Present Subjunctive is used in "that-clauses" that express a prayer, a wish, or a hope for a state of being that is not yet a reality. In formal the verb following "prayed that" or "wished that" must be in its base form (be), not the indicative form (is, am, or are).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The verb prayed acts as the trigger for the subjunctive mood in the subordinate clause. Even though the subject "son" is singular, the indicative verb is is incorrect in this formal context of a prayer. It must be replaced with the base form be to correctly reflect the subjunctive mood.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ They prayed that the rain cease before the harvest. (Not ceases)

Example 2 ✅ We pray that he be granted a swift recovery. (Not is)

Example 3 ✅ I pray that God bless you. (Not blesses)

questions.q_en:
Modern societies often celebrate progress through visible indicators—economic growth, technological penetration, and expanding infrastructure—while quietly overlooking fractures that resist quantification. Social inequality, though frequently acknowledged in rhetoric, is often treated as an abstract concern rather than a lived reality. The persistence of unequal access to education, healthcare, and legal recourse reveals that disparity is not merely a residual flaw of development but, in many cases, its unintended companion. Progress, when unevenly distributed, can deepen the very divides it claims to bridge. Public discourse tends to individualize social failure. Poverty is reframed as lack of effort, marginalization as absence of adaptability, and exclusion as personal deficiency. Such narratives offer moral comfort to the privileged by converting structural disadvantage into personal responsibility. Over time, this framing dulls collective urgency. When inequality is perceived as self-inflicted, social empathy is replaced by conditional sympathy—extended only to those deemed “deserving.” Institutions, meanwhile, respond with procedural solutions that emphasize efficiency over equity. Welfare systems grow increasingly conditional, access mechanisms become more complex, and accountability is measured through compliance rather than outcome. While these approaches appear neutral, they disproportionately burden those already navigating scarcity. The result is a paradoxical system in which assistance exists formally but remains functionally inaccessible to many. The most corrosive consequence of persistent inequality is not material deprivation alone but the erosion of social trust. When large sections of society experience the state as distant or indifferent, civic engagement weakens and resentment quietly accumulates. Addressing social issues, therefore, requires more than policy expansion; it demands a recalibration of how societies assign blame, distribute dignity, and define progress itself.

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The management expects the compliance team to submit the revised report by Monday.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The management expects the compliance team to submit the revised report by Monday.
options_en: The compliance team is expected to submit the revised report by Monday.
The revised report is expected that the compliance team will submit by Monday.
The revised report is expected to submit by the compliance team by Monday.
The compliance team was expected to be submitted the revised report by Monday.
options_hi: The compliance team is expected to submit the revised report by Monday.
The revised report is expected that the compliance team will submit by Monday.
The revised report is expected to submit by the compliance team by Monday.
The compliance team was expected to be submitted the revised report by Monday.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Infinitive Construction in Passive (Object + to-infinitive)

When an active sentence follows the structure: Subject + reporting verb (expect, believe, consider, want, order, allow, etc.) + object + to-verb, it can be converted into passive by making the object the subject, followed by the appropriate form of “be” + V³, while the infinitive remains unchanged. The correct passive structure becomes: Object + be + V³ + to + V¹.

Here, “expects” is the reporting verb, “the compliance team” is the object, and “to submit” is the infinitive.

In passive voice, the object (“the compliance team”) becomes the subject. Therefore, the correct structure is:

“The compliance team is expected to submit the revised report by Monday.”

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Identify the object before the infinitive. Make that object the subject in passive. Keep the infinitive in base form (to + V¹). Do not unnecessarily convert it into “to be + V³” unless meaning demands it. This structure is frequently tested with verbs like expect, believe, consider, report, and suppose in Banking and SSC Mains examinations.

Key Points

  • Nature of the Statement: The statement "The Mars rover captures new images... every day" represents a frequent action or a scientific fact that is still happening.

  • Rule for Permanent Truths: When the reported speech expresses a habitual action or a permanent truth, the tense of the verb (Simple Present: captures) does not change into the past (Simple Past: captured).

    • Option A incorrectly shifts the tense to "captured," implying the rover has stopped doing so.

    • Option C incorrectly shifts the tense to Past Perfect.

    • Option D incorrectly changes the reporting verb from "said" to "says."

questions.solution_en:

Here, “well” modifies the verb “spoke” and tells us how the diplomat spoke.

spoke how? → well

Therefore, “well” is an adverb.

options_en: He was grief-stricken when
he realized that his favorite
tree had been struck by lightning.
No Error
options_hi: He was grief-stricken when
he realized that his favorite
tree had been struck by lightning.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

📌 Rule / Concept: Struck vs. Stricken

Strike - Struck - Struck - Stricken (ADJECTIVE)

Struck (The Verb): This is the standard past participle (V3). It is used after auxiliary verbs (has, have, had, was, were) to indicate a completed action or a passive state.

Usage: Subject + was struck (passive) / Subject + has struck (active).

Example: The ship was struck by a giant wave.

Stricken (The Adjective): This is the "strong" participle form used primarily as an adjective. It is almost always used before a noun or in compound adjectives to describe a condition or a state of being overwhelmed.

Usage: A [Condition]-stricken + Noun.

Example: A poverty-stricken family; a panic-stricken crowd

💢 Analysis of the Question -

"He was grief-stricken (A) / when he realized that (B) / his favorite tree had been struck by lightning. (C)"

In Part A: "Grief-stricken" is used as a compound adjective to describe the man's emotional state. This is the correct adjectival use of the -en form.

In Part C: "Had been struck" is the passive voice (Past Perfect Passive). Since it is functioning as the main verb of the clause, the standard V3 form "struck" is exactly what is required.

The sentence correctly applies both forms in their appropriate grammatical slots.

📌 Rule / Concept: Interrogative Sentence (Yes/No Type) in Passive Voice

When a sentence is in interrogative form beginning with an auxiliary verb (Did/Do/Does/Has/Have/Will, etc.), the passive transformation follows this structure:

Auxiliary verb + object (new subject) + be (in correct tense) + V³

For simple past interrogatives starting with “Did,” the structure becomes: Was/Were + object + V³ ?

Because “Did + base verb” in active corresponds to “was/were + V³” in passive.

💢 Application to the Given Question - Here:

Auxiliary = Did (simple past)
Main verb = detect
Object = any discrepancies

In passive:
“any discrepancies” becomes the subject.
Since it is plural, we use “Were.”
Verb becomes past participle “detected.”
